option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded mutation points mutant chargen
option.helptext:
How many mutation points a Mutated Human starts character creation with.
Vanilla Caves of Qud gives 12. Caves of Qud Expanded has always given 16, which is the default here.
Set this before creating a character. Changing it has no effect on a character that already exists.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Mutated Human hit points per level
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded mutation hit points hp level mutant health
option.helptext:
How many hit points a Mutated Human rolls each time they gain a level. The range is rolled fresh every level, so a change takes effect from your next level onward.
{{G|1-5}} is what this mod has always documented: swingier than vanilla, with a higher ceiling, deliberately the opposite of the True Kin's steady {{G|2-4}}.
{{y|2-3}} is what version 2.2 actually shipped, through what appears to have been a mistake. It averages exactly what vanilla does and is strictly worse than the True Kin's range.
{{y|1-4}} is vanilla's.
True Kin and Psionic Adepts are unaffected either way.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: extra skill points per level
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded skill points level gain mutant true kin
option.helptext:
Grants the extra skill points per level this mod has always given: {{G|65}} for a Mutated Human against vanilla's 50, and {{G|85}} for a True Kin against vanilla's 70.
Turn this off to earn exactly vanilla's skill points.
Psionic Adepts are unaffected. Their {{G|95}} is the genotype rather than an addition to a vanilla one, so there is no vanilla number to fall back to.
Skill points are rolled at each level-up, so this takes effect from your next level. It does not take away points you have already earned.

option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded starting skills chargen cooking staunch wounds
option.helptext:
Grants Mutated Humans and True Kin the extra starting skills this mod has always given: Staunch Wounds, Cooking and Gathering, and Meal Preparation. Mutated Humans also get Menacing Stare.
Turn this off to start with exactly vanilla's skills. Vanilla's own starting skills are never removed.
Psionic Adepts are unaffected. Their starting skills are not an addition to a vanilla genotype - they are all the genotype has.
Set this before creating a character.

option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded skill requirements attribute axe cudgel long blade multiweapon tinkering
option.helptext:
Keeps the eased attribute requirements this mod has always used:
{{W|Axe}} and {{W|Cudgel}} accept {{G|Strength or Agility}} for every power, so an Agility build can buy Cleave, Berserk!, Slam and the rest. The numbers themselves are unchanged.
{{W|Long Blade}} lowers Dueling Stance to {{G|15}} Intelligence from 17, and En Garde! asks for 29 in Strength {{G|or}} Agility rather than 29 in one and 23 in the other.
{{W|Multiweapon Fighting}} lowers Expertise to {{G|21}} from 23 and Mastery to {{G|25}} from 27.
{{W|Tinkering}} lowers Tinker I to {{G|17}} Intelligence, II to {{G|21}} and III to {{G|25}}, from 19, 23 and 29.
Turn this off to face vanilla's requirements. No power is removed either way, and skills you already own are never taken back.
{{y|Takes effect when you restart the game.}} Qud builds each power's requirement list once and keeps it for the session.

option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded skill point cost tinkering cooking butchery spicer disassemble
option.helptext:
Keeps the skill point prices this mod has always used: {{W|Disassemble}} free rather than 100, {{W|Reverse Engineer}} {{G|200}} rather than 100, and {{W|Butchery}} and {{W|Spicer}} {{G|100}} each rather than 50.
The Cooking prices are an offset. This mod gives every genotype Cooking and Gathering and Meal Preparation for free at character creation, and charges more for the two powers above to pay for them. If you have turned {{W|extra starting skills}} off, you may want this off as well - otherwise you pay the offset without getting the skills it offsets.
Turn this off to pay exactly vanilla's prices. Powers you have already bought are unaffected.
This one applies immediately.

option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded starting reputation joppa faction chargen
option.helptext:
Gives Mutated Humans {{G|+300}} reputation with Joppa at character creation.
{{y|Off by default}}, unlike the rest of this mod. It grants power with nothing attached to use it, so it is the kind of change you should have to ask for rather than opt out of.
True Kin keep their vanilla Templar standing either way, and Psionic Adepts keep their Mechanimist standing.
Set this before creating a character.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: home base building in Joppa
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded joppa building home base becoming nook
option.helptext:
Adds a walled building near Argyve's workshop in Joppa: a bed, storage, an oven, and a becoming nook with a cybernetics rack.
{{y|Set this before starting a new character.}} Turning it off removes the building the next time you enter Joppa, and the ground beneath it is put back. Turning it back on afterwards does {{r|not}} rebuild it - the building is map data, and once removed from a save it is gone.
Nothing vanilla is removed either way.

option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded psionic chip drops loot artifact tables
option.helptext:
Lets psionic chips and chipsets appear in the world, as this mod has always done. They are rolled from the artifact tables at tiers 3 through 8, so they turn up in containers, on ruins floors and in merchants' stock alongside other artifacts.
Turn this off to play with the mod's weapons, armor and genotypes but none of the chip economy. No chip can be tinkered, so this closes the supply completely.
Fully live - this changes what is rolled from now on. Chips already lying in the world, or already in your pack, stay where they are.
Psionic Adepts still begin with their starting chips either way. Those are the genotype rather than an addition to it, and taking them would leave a subtype with nothing to use.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: your own Chip Interface slots
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded chip interface slot chargen psionic implant
option.helptext:
Gives your character the Chip Interface slots this mod has always granted: {{G|1}} for a Mutated Human and {{G|2}} for a True Kin. Chips implanted there grant mutations to genotypes that cannot otherwise mutate.
Turn this off to play with a vanilla body and no chip slots at all. Chips can still be found and traded, but you will have nowhere to implant them.
Psionic Adepts are unaffected. Their {{G|4}} slots are the genotype, not an addition to it, and removing them would leave it with nothing.
{{y|Set this before creating a character.}} A body is built once, at character creation, so this cannot change a character who already exists.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Chip Interface slots on other humanoids
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded chip interface npc humanoid anatomy world
option.helptext:
Gives every other humanoid in Qud a Chip Interface slot, as this mod has always done. The slot is merged into the base humanoid anatomy, so it reaches every villager, merchant and snapjaw at once.
Nothing in this mod ever puts a chip in an NPC's slot, so leaving this on has no effect you can see. Turn it off if you would rather other humanoids simply did not have the slot - for instance so that another mod, or a later version of this one, cannot start filling them.
Your own slots are controlled separately, by the option above.
{{y;Set this before creating a character.}} Bodies are built once, when a creature is generated, so this cannot change humanoids that already exist in a save.
